source.title: Known results and open problems in hypercomplex convexity

accepted.question_text: Let M^n be an n-dimensional manifold such that for every hyperplane L, the section M^n ∩ L is homeomorphic to the (n−1)-dimensional sphere S^{n−1}. Must M^n itself be homeomorphic to the n-dimensional sphere S^n?

evidence.quote:
Ulam problem. LetM n be n-dimensional manifold and every section of
M n by hyperplanes L be homeomorphic to (n− 1)-dimensional sphere Sn−1.
Is it true that M n is n-dimensional sphere?

In the real case this problem is solved by A. Kosi´ nski in 1962 [12]. The
repetition of this result was obtained by L. Montejano in 1990 [13]. In complex
case similar result was obtained by Yu. Zelinskii in 1993 [7].

accepted.question_text: Let C be a convex Jordan curve in the plane R^2 with the property that whenever three vertices of a rectangle abcd lie on C, the fourth vertex also lies on C. Must C be a circle?

evidence.quote:
Mizel problem (Characterization of a circle). Let C be a convex Jordan
curve on a plane R2 with the following property:
For every rectangle abcd, if any three vertices are on C, then the fourth
vertex will be also on C. Is it true that C is a circle?
This problem was solved by Besicovitch and Danzer independently [16, 17].

Suppose that the cohomology group H_j(K) is nonzero for some integer j ≥ 4. Must there then exist an index i with 1 ≤ i < j such that H_i(K) is also nonzero?

accepted.question_text: Let D be a bounded domain in hypercomplex Euclidean space H^n with smooth boundary, where n > 1. Assume D is locally linearly convex, meaning that for every boundary point z there exists a left hyperplane l and a neighborhood U(z) such that z ∈ l and D ∩ l ∩ U(z) = ∅. Must D then be H-convex, meaning that for every hypercomplex line γ the intersection γ ∩ D is acyclic, and must D be homeomorphic to the 4n-dimensional Euclidean ball R^{4n}?
